name: Ironwright Collective
description:
Ironwright Collective is not a label in any conventional sense — it has no offices, no registered corporate entity, no public-facing website or neural feed presence. It is a distributed network of approximately 300 active participants across GLMZ's Tier 1 and Tier 2 districts who manufacture, curate, and physically distribute music on data chips, vinyl pressings pressed in three different basement operations, and a hand-assembled zine format that includes liner notes, lyrics, and encrypted mesh addresses for listener communities. The Collective was founded in 2211 by a loose coalition of Shelf musicians, labor organizers, and former Lowline Press volunteers who felt that even independent labels with good intentions were still gatekeepers — that the only truly artist-controlled distribution was one where the artists themselves ran the infrastructure.

Ironwright releases are identified by a stamped iron insignia on physical media and a rotating 12-character mesh address that changes every 30 days to avoid corporate interception. The Collective has no A&R process — any artist in the network can submit a release, and if three members of the distribution circle vouch for it, it enters production. Releases are priced on a sliding scale, with Tier 1 listeners receiving copies at cost or free through a community voucher system funded by Tier 3 and Tier 4 buyers who pay a solidarity premium. The Collective's catalog skews heavily toward Shelf protest, raw neural punk, and what participants call 'witness music' — recordings made in and about specific places and moments in the lower tiers, meant to document what corporate media will not.
creator: Distributed founding collective (no single founder; key organizer known as Featherstone, identity undisclosed)
genre: Shelf protest, raw neural punk, witness music, Circuit folk, acoustic testimony, found-sound
audience: Tier 1 residents and organizers, Tier 2 workers with political consciousness, vinyl and data chip collectors, anti-corporate activists, underground journalists, anyone who distrusts centralized distribution
cultural_impact: Ironwright Collective has demonstrated that artist-controlled physical distribution at scale is possible in GLMZ, even under sustained corporate pressure. Its sliding-scale pricing model has been written about extensively in Circuit labor media as a template for post-corporate cultural economics. The Collective's releases — particularly its witness music catalog — are increasingly being sought by historians and archivists as primary sources documenting Shelf life during the 2210s, a period for which corporate media produced almost no coverage. Vantablack Media's legal team classifies Ironwright as a 'gray distribution entity' and pursues periodic enforcement actions, none of which have been effective.
known_fans: Shelf musicians and their immediate communities
Anti-corporate collectors who pay the solidarity premium
Tier 3 listeners who discovered the Collective through word of mesh
Rogue academics studying post-corporate music distribution
story_hooks: One of Ironwright's three vinyl pressing operations has been located by a Vantablack enforcement contractor. The Collective has 48 hours to move the equipment — several hundred kilograms of machinery, through Tier 1 streets, without attracting attention. The pressing operator, an older woman named Constance Adeyemi-Wolff, refuses to leave without her entire catalog archive.

A Tier 5 private collector has been quietly purchasing Ironwright releases through intermediaries and has now offered to fund a major expansion of the Collective's distribution infrastructure — anonymously, no strings attached. The Collective is divided: some see an opportunity, others see a trap, and a few suspect the offer is a Vantablack infiltration operation.

The encrypted mesh address rotation has failed — for the first time in Ironwright's history, the same address has been active for 60 days, and someone has been using the exposure to map the Collective's distribution nodes. The breach is internal. Someone in the vouching circle is feeding information out.
